text: What if Earth's spin doubled every 2 seconds?
say: What if Earth's spin doubled every two seconds?
formula: Title question word for word (STANDARD 1.3), rate in the title (0.13). Spin factor k(t) = 2^((t - 2 s)/2 s) (video time t; k = 1 before 2 s). Equator speed v = v0 x k with v0 = 2 x pi x 6,378.137 km / 86,164 s (sidereal day) = 465.1 m/s = 1,674 km/h. Day length shown = 24 h / k. Milestone times: t = 2 + 2 x log2(k).

text: You just want a slow sunset.
formula: Opening wish (STANDARD 0.14); paid off by n16.

text: Earth already spins you faster than sound.
formula: LEAN / reality first (2.11): at the equator you already move at 465 m/s = 1,674 km/h; speed of sound at 20 C = 343 m/s = 1,235 km/h. 465 > 343. On screen at k=2 (t=4 s): 930 m/s, faster than a typical rifle bullet (~900 m/s muzzle velocity).

text: Spin flings you outward. Faster spin, lighter you.
formula: SNAPBACK + physics (1.4). Centrifugal acceleration at the equator a = w^2 R = (2 pi/86,164)^2 x 6.378e6 m = 0.0339 m/s^2 = 0.346% of g (9.78 m/s^2 at the equator). It grows with k^2: weight loss f = 0.00347 x k^2. k=2: 1.4%; k=4: 5.5%; k=8: 22% lighter (t=8 s); k=12: 50% = half your weight (t=9.17 s).

text: Seventeen times faster. You weigh nothing.
formula: Weightless when f = 1: k = 1/sqrt(0.00347) = 17.0 (t = 2 + 2 log2 17 = 10.17 s). Then v = 465 x 17 = 7.9 km/s = orbital speed at the surface (first cosmic velocity), day = 23.93 h / 17 = 1.41 h = 1 h 24 min (widely cited 'about 84-minute day' for equatorial weightlessness).

text: So does the sea. It flies off into space.
formula: Water at the equator is not held down once k > 17; escape velocity from Earth's surface 11.19 km/s -> k = 11,186/465.1 = 24.05 (t = 11.18 s): it leaves Earth for good.

text: A real Earth would rip apart. Ours holds.
formula: Honest real-world limit (2.11): past k ~ 17 Earth's own gravity can no longer hold rock at the equator either, so a real Earth would break up. From here on, the solid Earth staying in one piece is the 'what if'.

text: You grab a palm tree. Mittens grabs you.
formula: Set-up for n12 and n15 (picture: you hanging 'up' from the palm trunk, Mittens on your shoe). On screen meanwhile: k=64 (t=14.0 s): 29.8 km/s, faster than Earth orbits the Sun (29.78 km/s); k=90.5 (t=15.0 s): 42.1 km/s = escape speed from the Sun at Earth's distance; k=144 (t=16.3 s): 1 day = 24 h/144 = 10 min.

text: Now faster than any spacecraft ever built.
formula: Parker Solar Probe, fastest human-made object: 191.7 km/s (692,000 km/h) at perihelion, 24 Dec 2024 (NASA). k = 191,700/465.1 = 412 -> t = 2 + 2 log2 412 = 19.37 s. On screen: k=287 (t=18.3 s): 1 day = 5 min; k=720 (t=21.0 s): 1 day = 2 min.

text: Fast enough to leave the Milky Way.
formula: Local escape speed of the Milky Way at the Sun's position ~ 550 km/s (Gaia DR2/DR3 estimates roughly 500-600 km/s, e.g. Deason et al. 2019: 528 km/s; Monari et al. 2018: 580 km/s). k = 550,000/465.1 = 1,183 -> t = 22.41 s.

text: You wanted a slow sunset. A day now lasts thirty seconds.
formula: Narrator against the hero (2.6), set up by n1. 1 day = 30 s when k = 86,400/30 = 2,880 -> t = 2 + 2 log2 2880 = 24.97 s (v = 1,340 km/s).

text: One percent of the speed of light.
You could let go. You don't.
formula: Narrator against the hero, set up by n7 (you hold on to the palm tree).

1 day = 3 s when k = 28,800 -> t = 31.64 s (v = 13,400 km/s = 4.5% of c). On screen before: k = 14,400 (t = 29.64 s): 1 day = 6 s. Real rotation angle shown = (2 pi/86,400 s) x integral of k dt = (2 pi/86,400) x (2/ln2) x (k - 1) rad: the first full sunset after the speed-up happens at about 28 s.

text: One day. One second. Mittens is still holding on.
formula: 1 day = 1 s when k = 86,400 -> t = 2 + 2 log2 86,400 = 34.81 s; v = 465.1 m/s x 86,400 = 40,200 km/s = 13% of c. Mittens-holding-on joke set up by n7.

text: Well. You did get a lot of sunsets.
formula: Callback ending paying off n1, said while it keeps speeding up. On screen: k = 161,180 (t = 36.60 s): 25% of c; k = 322,360 (t = 38.60 s): half the speed of light; k = 580,230 (t = 40.29 s): 90% of c. Last frame t = 40.5 s: k = 2^19.25 = 622,000, v = 289,000 km/s = 96% of c (still below c: k would reach c = 644,600 at t = 40.6 s; the video ends before that).
